$comment: Init profile manifest (spec 041). `spectastic init --profile <name>` composes principles.html + AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md from this data. Lives at the bundle root (read-only, like commands.json); never written to cwd. base = principles + AGENTS skeleton shared by every profile; each profile adds axis values, extra principles (deduped by name, appended after base with the next free P-number), and AGENTS lines. Advisory only — the enforcement teeth are spec 042.

principles.name: Clarity over cleverness
principles.statement: Prefer the simplest code the next reader — human or agent — can follow. Clever indirection is a cost, not a flex.

principles.name: Small, reversible changes
principles.statement: Ship in slices. Every change SHOULD be easy to revert; a large irreversible batch is a design smell.

principles.name: Explicit over implicit
principles.statement: Name things. No hidden magic, no action-at-a-distance an agent can't see from the code in front of it.

principles.name: One set of conventions, enforced
principles.statement: A single formatter and lint config, applied automatically. Style is decided once and enforced by the toolchain, not debated per PR.

principles.name: Record the why
principles.statement: Decisions carry their rationale. Code says what; a decision log or comment says why it had to be this way.

claudePointer: This project uses **AGENTS.md** as the canonical guide for coding agents.
Read [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) — it holds the setup commands, conventions, and the definition of done.
Keep project-specific agent guidance in AGENTS.md, not here, so every tool sees the same instructions.

agents: A change is done when it runs and a quick smoke check passes. Keep ceremony low; reach for more rigor only when the code earns it.

principles.name: Tests accompany behavior
principles.statement: Code that ships carries a test for the behavior it adds. The demoable path is covered before it merges.

principles.name: Contract-first interfaces
principles.statement: A component that exposes an interface ships a checked-in contract (OpenAPI, JSON Schema, or a typed signature) before the code behind it. The contract is the agent's target and the consumer's guarantee.

principles.name: Library-first boundaries
principles.statement: Keep the reusable core separate from its entry point. Logic lives in a testable, importable library; the CLI, endpoint, or UI is a thin adapter over it.

principles.name: Secure by default
principles.statement: Safe defaults are the floor: no hardcoded credentials, secrets from the environment, authorization on by default. Every insecurity is an explicit, reviewed exception, never an accident.

principles.name: Least privilege
principles.statement: Grant the narrowest capability that does the job — to a service, a token, and an autonomous agent alike. Bound the blast radius before you widen the access.

principles.name: Done means verified
principles.statement: Every level of testing is produced — unit, integration, and a behavioral check that exercises the running code. Where no framework exists, build a minimal tool to self-verify. Presence is never accepted as proof.

principles.name: The enforcement floor holds
principles.statement: When a gate tool fails — a version incompatibility, a new toolchain, a false positive — fix the gate (bump the tool, adjust its config, pin a known-good version) before removing it. Disabling or loosening a gate is a last resort that is explicit and recorded, never a silent convenience.

agents: A change is done only when: every level is verified (unit + integration + behavioral + a soak/perf check for hot paths); a change to an already-working app ships behind a feature toggle, off by default (standing the app up the first time is not gated); dependencies pass a supply-chain scan; and every design decision cites its evidence.

Apply the practices a staff engineer would by reflex: pin dependency versions, gate on a security + supply-chain scan, and enforce project invariants with custom rules wired into CI — never restated in prose.
If a rule you need to enforce has no tool in this ecosystem, build a minimal checker and block CI on it.

The enforcement floor holds: when a pinned gate tool breaks against your toolchain (e.g. a static analyzer on a newer JDK/runtime), bump it or fix its config before disabling it — do not switch off a gate as the first response. Any deliberate weakening is explicit and recorded.
